## 1. International Monetary Fund mission begins two‑week review of Sri Lanka’s programme and economy.

The mission will run from <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">10 to 23 September</span> and fold the seventh review of the Extended Fund Facility (a four‑year support package that disburses money in tranches against reforms) into the annual <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Article IV consultation</span> (the IMF’s regular health check on a member’s economy). The previous combined fifth and sixth reviews in May unlocked about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$695 million</span>, taking total disbursements to roughly <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$2.4 billion</span> while keeping the $3 billion headline envelope intact.

Attention now turns to revenue performance, debt‑service capacity and the fiscal path for 2027, when grace periods begin to fade. Domestic interest costs still absorb more than a third of spending, while foreign‑currency interest, though declining from an estimated $1.09 billion in 2025 to a projected $0.93 billion in 2026, remains a steady drain on reserves.

## 2. Parliament votes to abolish the post of Chief of Defence Staff.

The repeal bill cleared the second reading on <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">9 September</span> <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">without a division</span> after a six‑hour debate. With the law’s commencement, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">property belonging to the disbanded office</span> will transfer to the Ministry of Defence, and tri‑service coordination will revert to existing command arrangements.

The position, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">created in 2009</span> to align the armed forces with wartime requirements, had become an institutional overlap as peacetime structures matured. Legislators opted for streamlining rather than re‑engineering, a choice that will be tested by how joint operations are handled during disasters and large‑scale security events.

## 3. Cabinet clears publication of a new Prevention of Organised Crime Bill.

The draft drew the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Attorney General’s clearance</span> and will be gazetted before being tabled in the House. It is framed to domesticate the UN Convention against Transnational Organised Crime (<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">UNTOC</span>, a global treaty to fight cross‑border rackets) and to create tools for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">asset seizure</span>, cross‑border cooperation and modern evidence handling that routine criminal law lacks.

Officials signalled the statute would end the practice of detaining gang suspects under counter‑terrorism provisions by giving prosecutors a tailored route to charge serious rackets. Safeguards and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">non‑retroactivity</span> are to be written in, and separate bilateral tracks are being pursued to repatriate fugitives.

## 4. A 350 MW combined‑cycle power plant wins Board of Investment registration.

The Kerawalapitiya project, registered on 13 August under <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Section 17(2)</span> of the BOI law, carries a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$291.19 million</span> outlay and will run on diesel initially before switching to regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG, natural gas converted to liquid for transport and then returned to gas) as the national supply chain comes on stream. Built on a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">BOOT basis</span> (build‑own‑operate‑transfer), it is split into a 243 MW gas turbine phase and a 107 MW steam unit, the configuration that defines a combined‑cycle plant (a system that uses waste heat from a gas turbine to drive a steam turbine, raising efficiency).

When fully staffed, the facility expects to support <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">1,147 jobs</span> and lift the Kerawalapitiya cluster’s capacity to around 1,000 MW alongside Sobadhanavi and Yugadhanavi. The 42‑month schedule now becomes the grid planner’s benchmark for bridging a dry‑season hydro shortfall at the lowest fuel cost.

## 5. Container congestion at Colombo’s deep‑draft berths is set to persist for at least two weeks.

Turnaround at the largest‑vessel berths has stretched to as much as <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">six days</span> as cargo displaced from Gulf hubs converges on a narrow set of deep‑water windows. One main terminal is working through an inter‑terminal transfer backlog of around <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">35,000 TEUs</span> while strong winds have intermittently slowed pilotage and tug operations.

Even so, throughput grew <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">7.3% year‑on‑year</span> in July to 774,513 TEUs, with transhipment up 8.4% and the port climbing to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">20th place globally</span> on first‑half volumes. The rub is mix rather than volume: re‑stows and relay boxes now account for 85% of moves, leaving exporters reliant on schedule reliability being restored.

## 6. Supreme Court voids 2010 fast‑track police promotions as unconstitutional.

A three‑judge bench held that Cabinet decisions elevating three Chief Inspectors to Assistant Superintendent outside the recruitment scheme breached equal‑treatment guarantees under <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Article 12(1)</span>. The rulings <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">annulled the decisions</span> and the Inspector General’s circular that implemented them, restoring the principle that merit and process govern advancement.

The applications, lodged by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">33 officers</span>, turn on a familiar fault line: <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">ad‑hoc political preferment</span> versus structured career paths. The judgment signals that even decade‑old personnel moves remain vulnerable if they departed from the rules.

## 7. Government creates Digital Transformation Units across ministries and agencies.

The new units, headed by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Chief Digital Officers</span> reporting to institutional heads, will coordinate sectoral digitisation and enforce the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">National Digital Commons</span> (a shared standards stack for public services). <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">GovTech Sri Lanka</span> will backstop with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, interoperability and AI/data advisory, aiming to end fragmented projects and vendor lock‑ins.

The move operationalises the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2025–2030</span> national digital economy plan and gives a clear line of accountability for delivering e‑procurement, paperless workflows and citizen‑facing platforms.

## 8. Online monthly railway season tickets open to private‑sector commuters from 1 October.

The facility, previously limited to public servants, will run through the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">seat‑reservation portal</span> once a user account and identity are verified at a booking‑enabled station. The change ends the 10‑day, mid‑day application window and repeat counter visits that made renewals costly in time for workers.

The step forms part of a wider digitisation push that also includes a pilot smart‑ticketing system on the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Kelani Valley line</span> and the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">RDMNS app</span> for live operational updates.

## 9. Telecom tower company commits $10 million to expand shared network infrastructure.

EDOTCO’s 30‑month plan covers <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">130 macro towers</span>, 300 smart lamp poles and 650 energy sites, adding to roughly 950 poles and 800 sites already deployed. The licence now also permits the development of fibre, in‑building systems, data centres and active network solutions, widening the toolkit for densifying coverage.

Cumulative investment will rise to about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">$40 million</span> since 2016, a bet on accelerating demand from AI, streaming and the State’s digital‑services agenda.

## 10. Sri Lanka dispatches $1 million in humanitarian support to Nepal after floods and landslides.

The funds, handed over in Kathmandu on <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">9 September</span>, will feed into relief and recovery in districts such as <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading</span> after a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">glacial burst</span> sent debris surging downriver. The gesture follows diplomatic engagement and aligns with the country’s use of targeted aid to reinforce regional ties.

Kathmandu’s disaster agency has recorded heavy loss of life and missing persons, underscoring the scale of needs relative to bilateral allocations.
